Somerville.narrative: Somerville's market remains exceptionally tight across all property types, with condos leading the charge as the most competitive segment — half of all condo sales are closing above asking price at a median of $1,007,500, and with 52 units sold in the last 30 days, it's clearly the most active category in the city. Single families are commanding a median of $1,175,000 at 97.9% of list price with 25% selling over ask, while multi-families are fetching a median of $1,300,000 with a third of sales going above list — a strong signal of continued investor and owner-occupant demand for income-producing properties. With effectively no months of supply reported across all three segments, this is about as inventory-starved as a market can get. Sellers are in a commanding position with near-guaranteed strong offers and minimal days on market, while buyers should expect to move fast, come in at or above list price, and have financing airtight before stepping foot at an open house.

Cambridge.narrative: Cambridge remains one of the most fiercely competitive markets in Greater Boston, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $2,460,000 and an astonishing 104.2% sale-to-list ratio — 80% of those homes selling above asking price in the last 30 days alone. The condo market, while slightly more accessible at a $1,050,000 median, still saw 42.2% of its 83 closed sales go over list price, signaling relentless demand across all price points. Multi-family properties are moving at a $2,045,375 median with a 98.5% SP/LP ratio, attracting both investors and owner-occupants drawn to Cambridge's rental strength and long-term appreciation story. With effectively no months of supply across all property types, sellers hold enormous leverage and should expect multiple offers, while buyers need to come in pre-approved, waiver-ready, and prepared to move aggressively above list price to have any realistic chance of winning.

Medford.narrative: Medford's real estate market is firing on all cylinders, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $961,000 and selling at 104.7% of list price — a striking 76.5% of those homes selling above asking, signaling intense buyer competition across the city. Condos are holding steady at a $800,000 median with an even sale-to-list ratio, though more than half are still going over ask, while multi-families are leading the pack at $1,168,000 median with 60% selling above list at 102.6% SP/LP. With essentially zero months of supply across all property types and only 37 total sales in the past 30 days, inventory is critically tight, leaving buyers with little room to negotiate and virtually no time to deliberate. Sellers in Medford are in an exceptionally strong position right now — properly priced listings are generating immediate, competitive offers — making this one of the most landlord- and seller-favorable conditions the metro has seen in recent memory.

Melrose.narrative: Melrose continues to demonstrate fierce demand across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,031,800 and an eye-popping 82.6% of those 23 sales closing above asking price at an average of 107.5% of list price. Multi-family properties are equally competitive, with a median sale of $1,208,000 and two-thirds of the 6 transactions going over ask, while condos offer a comparatively accessible entry point at $512,500, though half of those deals still exceeded list price. With essentially no measurable months of supply across all three segments, inventory is critically thin, meaning sellers hold enormous leverage and can realistically expect multiple offers and strong premiums above their asking price. For buyers, Melrose demands aggressive preparation — pre-approval in hand, waived contingencies on the table, and the flexibility to move quickly — as hesitation in this market almost certainly means losing out.

Arlington.narrative: Arlington's housing market is firing on all cylinders across every property type, with single-family homes commanding a median of $1,217,000 and closing at 105.5% of list price — 70.6% of them selling above asking — while multi-families are the most competitive segment of all, with 83.3% selling over ask at a striking 109.6% sale-to-list ratio and a median of $1,405,000. Condos, though comparatively tamer at 100% of list price, still saw 40% of units sell above asking with a median of $880,000, and with effectively zero months of supply across all categories, inventory remains a critical constraint. For sellers, Arlington is about as favorable as it gets — well-priced listings are generating multiple offers and meaningful premiums with minimal time on market. Buyers should come prepared with pre-approvals locked, escalation clauses ready, and realistic expectations of waiving contingencies, as hesitation in this market almost certainly means losing out.

Belmont.narrative: Belmont's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes posting a median sale price of $1,451,000 and 75% of properties selling over asking price at an average of 104.2% of list price — a clear signal that demand is dramatically outpacing supply. Multi-family properties are actually seeing even more aggressive bidding, with a sale-to-list ratio of 105.9% and three out of four selling above ask at a median of $1,415,500, reflecting strong investor and owner-occupant interest in this transit-friendly community. Condos offer a comparatively softer entry point at $775,000 with only 33.3% selling over ask, though a 99% sale-to-list ratio confirms there's little room for negotiation even in that segment. For sellers, this is an exceptional moment to list with virtually no inventory sitting on the market, while buyers should arrive fully pre-approved, waiver-ready, and prepared to move decisively — hesitation in Belmont right now is costly.

Watertown.narrative: Watertown's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $975,000 and 66.7% of properties selling above asking price at a 100.1% sale-to-list ratio — a clear signal that buyer demand is far outpacing available inventory. Condos offer a relatively more accessible entry point at a $695,230 median with an even split of 50% selling over ask, while multi-family properties are the hottest segment, fetching a median of $1,325,000 with 66.7% over ask and a 101.1% SP/LP ratio. With effectively zero months of supply reported across all categories and only 38 total transactions in the past 30 days, inventory is critically constrained. Sellers are in an exceptionally strong position to command top dollar with minimal concessions, while buyers should expect to compete aggressively, come in at or above list price, and move quickly with clean, well-prepared offers.

Winchester.narrative: Winchester's single-family market is firing on all cylinders, with a median sale price of $1,523,575 and homes closing at 101.2% of list price — 60% of them selling above asking in the last 30 days. The condo segment is even more competitive, with a median of $971,500, a 103.7% sale-to-list ratio, and a striking 75% of units trading over ask. With effectively zero months of supply across both property types and 28 combined sales in the past month, inventory is essentially nonexistent, giving sellers extraordinary leverage to price confidently and attract multiple offers. For buyers, Winchester demands sharp pre-approval, swift decision-making, and a willingness to stretch above list price — hesitation in this market almost certainly means losing out.

Boston.narrative: Boston's real estate market remains intensely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $922,000 and selling at 101.1% of list price — with nearly 57% of homes closing above asking, signaling fierce buyer competition. Condos, the most active segment with 366 sales in the past 30 days, are moving at a median of $800,000 and a 99.5% sale-to-list ratio, while multi-families lead in price at $1,175,000 with 42.9% selling over ask. With effectively zero months of supply across all three property types, inventory is critically constrained, leaving buyers facing bidding wars and little room to negotiate regardless of which segment they're targeting. For sellers, conditions couldn't be more favorable — properly priced homes are essentially selling at or above list price with strong velocity, making this an ideal time to bring a property to market.
